newsitem.title: CHINA: China says full currency convertibility needs time.
newsitem.headline: China says full currency convertibility needs time.

text.p: China still needs a "fairly long period" before making its currency convertible on the capital account, central bank governor Dai Xianglong said.
The governor of the People's Bank of China said the renminbi was in effect already convertible on the current account.
"As for the capital account, this will need a fairly long period," he told Reuters Editor-in-Chief Mark Wood in an interview on Tuesday.
"We will in future take an active and prudent attitude," he said. "We are still working on it but there is no timetable."
China has been dismantling its curbs on the currency's conversion, removing in July restrictions on current account sales of foreign exchange to foreign enterprises.
It has promised to make full convertibility on the current account by the end of the year.
A central bank spokesman repeated that pledge on Wednesday, saying Beijing would comply with convertibility requirements for the current account under International Monetary Fund Article 8.
The move would not mean much change from current practice, he told reporters, although he added that preparations had to be made for its implementation.
He said Beijing was ahead of schedule as far as its convertibility programme was concerned.
